why_relevant: Internal auditors' institute running certification (incl. 'Ovlašćeni računovođa') and training; lecturer and member lists identify risk/compliance practitioners inside Montenegrin banks - a soft actor map for governance and AML topics.

source_name: Institut sertifikovanih računovođa Crne Gore (ISRCG) — Q&A and practice guidance
why_relevant: Professional body whose Q&A surfaces practitioner-level detail on filing deadlines, form quirks and exemptions — invaluable for interpreting ME statutory accounts correctly and for spotting entity classes that escape filing.
Third-party normaliser of Montenegroberza listings and historical instrument prices; useful cross-check and continuity when the exchange's own archive is reorganised.

source_name: thebanks.eu – Montenegro bank profiles (asset rankings and market share)
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator giving comparable total-assets and market-share rankings per Montenegrin bank in English; useful for prioritising which bank IR sites to poll most often and for cross-checking self-reported figures. Secondary source — never a substitute for the bank's own PDF.

source_name: Cuspera vendor customer-story aggregator (Temenos and peers)
why_relevant: Aggregates published vendor customer stories in one searchable place, cheaper to sweep than crawling every core-banking vendor site individually. Serves as a discovery net for any future ME core-banking reference.

Domestic .me tender listing surfaced alongside the official portal in local-language search; potential secondary mirror for ME notices. Low prior on completeness and unclear operator, so it is a lead to evaluate rather than a trusted feed.
Aggregates S&P/Moody's/Fitch/DBRS/Scope actions on ME with outlooks and dates; a third redundancy layer for rating-event detection.

Secondary Montenegrin portal that carries named-official economic statements (e.g. minister/CBCG commentary on economic activity). Useful as a redundancy channel and for catching quotes that dailies trim, though it largely mirrors wire copy.

source_name: Kriptobroker.me — self-described first crypto brokerage in Montenegro
why_relevant: Non-bank crypto-side actor announcing consumer-facing exchange and (claimed) point-of-sale crypto acceptance. Weak signal for alternative merchant acceptance rails ahead of MiCA-aligned Montenegrin legislation.

source_name: Montenegro Business Alliance (MBA / Montenegro Biznis Alijansa)
why_relevant: Umbrella private-sector advocacy organisation founded 2001 in Podgorica, historically active on tax and regulatory policy. No live own-domain site was located in this pass, so third-party organisation records are currently the only handle; worth a periodic re-check because its position papers would be in scope.

Local-language business directory listing Montenegrin banks with contact and site links. Low editorial value but useful as a snowball surface for local-language bank name spellings and for finding smaller institutions and MFIs missing from English lists.

source_name: Prekoveze.me — employer job-ad pages (e.g. Crnogorska komercijalna banka)
why_relevant: Employer-scoped ME job aggregator that keeps a per-bank page with dated vacancies, giving an easy longitudinal hiring series per institution.

source_name: Schmidt & Schmidt — official extracts from the Montenegrin commercial register and accounting statements
why_relevant: Service that procures certified ME registry extracts and filed accounting statements for named companies — a practical, legally clean fallback when the primary portals are certificate-gated or TLS-broken.
